title: Sell Mineral Rights in McGregor, ND
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in McGregor, ND
metaDescription: Own mineral rights near McGregor, ND in Williams County? This small community sits in strong Bakken core acreage. Get an honest offer.
heroLead: McGregor is barely a dot on the map, an unincorporated community rather than a town with its own city hall, but the mineral rights tied to this stretch of Williams County sit in genuinely productive Bakken ground.
intro: Families who trace their mineral ownership back to the original homestead near McGregor have generally watched the same story play out as most of Williams County: quiet farmland for generations, then a wave of leasing and horizontal drilling after the mid-2000s, and now mature wells settling into a longer decline. What that means for your specific interest depends on exactly which wells are tied to your acreage.

sections.heading: Small community, strong underlying rock
paragraphs: Being unincorporated doesn't say anything about what's under the ground. Williams County's core Bakken acreage runs through this area, and we've seen McGregor-area interests with solid multi-well production. We check the state's well index against your legal description rather than judge by the community's size.

sections.heading: What we need to get started
paragraphs: A recent royalty statement, an old deed, or a Division Order gives us what we need to confirm your ownership through the Williams County Recorder and identify the wells tied to your interest before we make an offer.

sections.heading: Reading a McGregor-area royalty statement
paragraphs: Statements from wells near McGregor often reflect production pooled across a multi-well pad, which can make the math confusing if you're only used to seeing a single well's numbers. Gathering, processing, and marketing deductions are usually itemized separately from the gross value before your net payment is calculated.

We can walk through your specific statement line by line so you understand exactly what's driving the check you receive, and whether the trend is flat, rising with new infill activity, or settling into a longer decline.

faqs.question: McGregor isn't really a town. Does that affect our mineral rights' value?
faqs.answer: No, value is driven by the underlying well production and acreage location, not the size or status of the nearest community.

faqs.question: We don't have any recent paperwork. Can you still find our interest?
faqs.answer: Yes, with a legal description from any old deed we can research your ownership directly through the Williams County Recorder's records.

faqs.question: Is Williams County still actively being drilled?
faqs.answer: Yes, it remains one of the most active counties in the play, though specific activity near your tract varies and we check that directly.

faqs.question: How do you handle a mineral interest with several unnamed co-owners?
faqs.answer: We research the full ownership chain through county records and can work with each co-owner individually or coordinate a combined sale, whichever your family prefers.
